The '''2020–21''' season was '''[[Liverpool F.C.|Liverpool Football Club]]''''s [[List of Liverpool F.C. seasons|129th season]] in existence and their 59th consecutive season in the top flight of [[Football in England|English football]]. In addition to the [[2020–21 Premier League|domestic league]], Liverpool participated in this season's editions of the [[2020–21 FA Cup|FA Cup]], the [[2020–21 EFL Cup|EFL Cup]], the [[2020 FA Community Shield|FA Community Shield]] and the [[2020–21 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]]. The season covered the period from August 2020 to 30 June 2021. This was the first season since [[2013–14 Liverpool F.C. season|2013–14]] without [[Dejan Lovren]], who departed to [[Zenit Saint Petersburg]] and [[Adam Lallana]], who departed to [[Brighton and Hove Albion F.C.|Brighton and Hove Albion]].

==Season overview==
The season was notably difficult, as the majority of games were played [[Behind closed doors (sport)|behind closed doors]] due to the [[COVID-19 pandemic in England|COVID-19 pandemic]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/fans/behind-closed-doors/home|title=Reds Behind Closed Doors 20/21|work=Liverpool FC|access-date=26 May 2021}}</ref> and all three of the club's senior central defenders sustained long-term injuries.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/first-team/424517-jurgen-klopp-confirms-joel-matip-injury-diagnosis|title=Jürgen Klopp confirms Joel Matip injury diagnosis|date=1 February 2021|work=Liverpool FC|access-date=26 May 2021}}</ref> The team's early form was creditable and, on 22 November 2020, they broke the club record for longest unbeaten run at home in the league (which had previously stood at 63) with a 3–0 win over [[Leicester City F.C.|Leicester City]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2020/nov/22/liverpool-leicester-premier-league-match-report|title=Jota strikes again as Liverpool ease to record-breaking win over Leicester|date=22 November 2020|work=The Guardian|accessdate=17 February 2021}}</ref> However, the run ended on 21 January 2021 following a 1–0 defeat to [[Burnley F.C.|Burnley]]; it had stood at 68, the second-longest unbeaten home run in English top-flight history, behind [[Chelsea F.C.|Chelsea]]'s run of 86 games between March 2004 and October 2008, and the longest under a single manager.<ref>{{cite web|url= https://www.skysports.com/football/live-blog/11661/12191694/liverpool-vs-burnley-live|title= Liverpool 0–1 Burnley highlights|date=21 January 2021|work=Sky Sports|accessdate=9 March 2021}}</ref> A tough period followed as Liverpool suffered a run of six consecutive defeats at Anfield.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.premierleague.com/match/59160|title=Lemina strike earns Fulham victory at Liverpool|date=7 March 2021|work=Premier League|access-date=26 May 2021}}</ref> This ended any chance the team had of retaining the Premier League title as by early March, Liverpool sat 8th in the table with 43 points. The team, however, was able to reverse their fortunes, winning eight of their final ten league games, which included goalkeeper [[Alisson Becker]] scoring a stoppage-time winner against [[West Bromwich Albion F.C.|West Bromwich Albion]] (the first goal ever scored by a Liverpool goalkeeper in the 129-year history of the club),<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/57044633|title=West Bromwich Albion 1–2 Liverpool|date=16 May 2021|work=BBC|access-date=26 May 2021}}</ref> meaning they finished third with 69 points, qualifying for the next season's [[2021–22 UEFA Champions League|UEFA Champions League]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.theguardian.com/football/2021/may/23/liverpool-crystal-palace-premier-league-match-report|title=Mané seals third place for Liverpool with double against Crystal Palace|date=23 May 2021|work=The Guardian|access-date=26 May 2021}}</ref>

==Pre-season friendlies==
On 19 August 2020, Liverpool announced that they would play two friendlies as part of their pre-season training camp in [[Austria]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Reds to play friendlies against Stuttgart and Salzburg |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/first-team/405769-reds-to-play-friendlies-against-stuttgart-and-salzburg |publisher=Liverpool F.C. |access-date=20 August 2020}}</ref> On 2 September 2020, they announced that they would complete their pre-season campaign with a home game against [[Blackpool F.C.|Blackpool]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Liverpool to face Blackpool in pre-season friendly |url=https://www.liverpoolfc.com/news/first-team/407276-liverpool-to-face-blackpool-in-pre-season-friendly |publisher=Liverpool F.C. |access-date=29 May 2021}}</ref>
